And since I didn't get around to doing a write up last time, here's an Asian Drama to make up for it! ːsteamsunnyː

~~Asian Drama~~

~~Because You Totally Know You Care~~

[previewyoutube=6j9Jvigm52k;full][/previewyoutube]
The Asian Drama this time around is called "Kill You Love You" and...the title is very uncreative, but it's still a pretty sweet show. Above is the mondo, compiled cut of all of the episodes, but if you want to watch the episodes in more manageable, bite sized chunks, the [url=https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLIPiKkS-FpK_Q5iFP6FGJofqldQESqWi3]playlist for that is here.[/url]

The story, from what I can remember, is this... There is a Prince who is investigating the suspicious death of his late father, and is building an undercover army so he can rightfully take the throne back from the corrupt empress. But in order to throw suspicion off of him, he pretends to be a notorious womanizer so that he can build and strategize in peace, while everyone thinks he's off with some lady. Meanwhile, the leading lady is an assassin, who is charged with protecting him...but she doesn't get the memo, so she ends up trying to kill him instead. (Whoops.)

I'm not exactly sure what the "correct" terminology for this show format is, but this seems to be a mini-series? All the episodes are really short, so even though there's a lot of them, you can get through them fairly quickly, and at your own pace. (Similar to [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/355520/announcements/detail/3653029702859369691?snr=2___]No Doubt in Us[/url].) What I like about this format of T.V. Show is that I never feel like my time is being wasted. With the full-blown, 45 minute episodes of regular Chinese Dramas, the plot just drags its feet in getting anywhere, so nothing truly happens until Episode 15. Which sucks and is annoying. However, with these kinds of shows, where the episodes are around 10 minutes each, the writing has to make the most of its short runtime, so even if they don't get to the point immediately, [i]they still get there a lot faster than they do in the regular shows...![/i] (This doesn't always translate into good writing, but sometimes you'll be pleasantly surprised...!)

This show in particular I like for a few reasons. First of all, the main character seems like another generic stoic guy, but deep down he's a big sweetie. Second, since this story is from his perspective (and I suspect written by a man as well, but can't confirm) he comes across as a lot more sympathetic. He isn't this plank of wood, staring off blankly with nothing going on; he's a guy who's pretending to be someone he's not so that he can honour the legacy of his late father. He's purposefully guarded, not bland, and that may be subtle, but it makes a difference.

The assassin lady...is charming enough, from what I can remember. (It's been a while since I watched this show.) Her demeanor is believable for an assassin, and while she does seem to be clumsier than she should be at times (and a bit too petite to be believably athletic), she's not annoying or disrespectful towards the male lead.

Though, one thing I didn't particular like was [spoiler]how she reacted when she found out that the male lead was secretly engaged the whole time. Granted, that kind of news would rile any woman up, but he made it clear that it was an arranged marriage, he never met the other woman, and he had no feelings for her. I don't think it was fair for the script to blame the main guy, and then "comedically" punish him for something he had absolutely no control over. Main bro didn't deserve that.[/spoiler]

So, yeah! That's my recommendations for this time around, and I hope you have a great Autumn coming up! :D :D :D Buh-bye!

~~Asian Drama Recommendation You Are Totally, 100% Invested In~~
If you're going to spending Valentines Day alone like I am, then why not pick up on something light and fluffy to watch? This time I'm recommending [url=https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLIPiKkS-FpK_Cmpo7tK7FWD4CAQ8U7yoW]Wrong Carriage Right Groom[/url], because that one was a fun one that really surprised me! The title pretty much gives away the basic premise, but here I go anyway... XD

The story takes place in Ye Olde China (as a lot of these Asian Dramas I watch, do), where two women are getting married to guys they don't want to marry. One is a firecracker warrior babe who doesn't like being told what to do, and the other is a calm, stoic, thoughtful gal who is getting married as a means to sacrificially save her family from doom. On their way to their weddings in different towns, they get caught in a fierce rainstorm which causes them both to accidentally switch places and get toted off to the wrong town as well as the wrong groom. Firecracker girl ends up marrying the guy the calm gal was supposed to marry (a sickly guy with bad luck [spoiler]who is actually completely faking it[/spoiler]), and calm gal ends up getting the guy that firecracker girl was supposed to marry (a widower general who [strike]looks like [url=https://youtu.be/miD_TWmdGIY?si=1pbfkpsc-5RSamkD&t=66]Steven He[/url][/strike] has had two wives already before [spoiler]who died due to reasons completely beyond his control[/spoiler]). Which ends up being just fine by them, because they were kind of dreading the guys they were supposed to marry, and are much happier with their accidental husbands instead.

A couple things I like about this show. First of all, it doesn't have any of that annoying will-they-won't-they nonsense that is grating more and more on my nerves when I watch TV Shows nowadays. The girls already have their designated love interests, and apart from a couple of hiccups, it stays that way from beginning to end. Therefore, the majority of the story [b]actually focuses on something new and interesting.[/b]

Second thing I appreciate is that there's no real "boy vs. girl" dynamics in the relationships. You would expect Little Miss Firecracker to be super domineering (which she is) and walk all over Sickly Guy, but he actually ends up being the dominant figurehead in their relationship. Why? [b]Because he's smart and she listens to him.[/b] There's no arguing, there's no childish conversations about who should be in charge, there's just a silent understanding between them that they need to work together to accomplish their goals. And if that means letting the other person be in charge when it's appropriate, then so be it. The same goes for Calm Gal and General Guy--he lets her lead many times because he realizes that she is really good at thinking outside the box. But they're overall the more mellow couple of the show, so it's less noticeable.

That's not to say this show is without flaws, though. The fact that the main couples get together so easily, and that everything's so pleasant so early on, almost made me drop the show at one point, because I already felt satisfied with the status quo. I [i]did[/i] keep going, and I'm glad I did, but it was definitely tempting to dip out at one point out of content-boredom.

The main reason I recommended this show for Valentine's Day is because it is, what I like to call, "Shipper Happy"--in that it's Trigger Happy with its ships. Apart from a couple of throwaway extras and a Eunuch, every character introduced is given a love interest. There are of course the two main couples, which are a given, but then there are these doctor characters who act as mentors, and what do you know? [spoiler]They happen to be long lost lovers and they get back together![/spoiler] Like...it was sweet, but it didn't feel earned? [spoiler]I would have preferred it if they were the one couple in the show that didn't get together right away, and waited until the very end to reconcile their differences.[/spoiler] But as abrupt as [i]that pairing[/i] was, it was not as bad as the random Princess that is randomly introduced halfway through because [spoiler]that one lovable side character needed a love interest.[/spoiler] Sure. Why not? XD

Also, according to some of the comments I read, this show is a remake of a much older show of the same name. I can't tell you which version was better, but I thought the version I did watch, was cute, so that's the one I'm recommending. ;3

Despite its flaws, though, it's still a really fun watch. I didn't even get to the really sweet granny, and the story of the one designated evil couple, but I'll leave that intrigue for if you decide to watch the show. ;) Overall, a really lighthearted and fun experience about how sometimes little mix-ups can result in greater things happening.

Happy Valentines Day for those who are celebrating with someone they love and those who aren't! <3 <3 <3

In Ye Olde Ancient China, there is a a cute little girl who applies to become the Imperial Coroner (Roll Credits~), and because she seems to have a real knack for it, she gets the job. The prince, however, suspects something sinister is afoot, because of a bunch of mysterious deaths that keep happening to political opponents and the like. So together, the Prince and the newly appointed Coroner begin to unravel this web of political intrigue through investigating all the various assassinations that they come across!

The most unrealistic thing about this show is how up-to-date the medical knowledge is. The main characters' detailed knowledge of human anatomy, fractures, and all sorts of things is kind of distracting when you think about the fact that they should be using Ye Olde Chinese Leeches or something to solve all their problems. But, otherwise, the show is quite enjoyable, if a little hard to follow in the beginning.

Also, there is no Love-Triangle Nonsense going on. Most of the characters are just focused on doing their jobs, and when romance comes up, there's a little bit of "will-they-won't-they" that shows up, but it's usually resolved pretty quickly. The two male characters are both pretty cool guys, and when a girl-boss-ish character shows up later, she's not annoying and is actually useful to the plot. :)

This one is more of a mystery series than the other Asian Dramas I've recommended, and it's kind of Halloweeny, what with the talk of dead people. So, if you're in the mood to binge a great show, then this is the one for you! :D

Lastly, I'd like to include this song from the Dreamworks Prequel Sequel to Prince of Egypt, Joseph: King of Dreams. I remember rewatching this movie as an adult and thinking it was nothing special. But then I went through a really hard time in my life, and this movie was right there. It's not perfect (due to budget cuts and troubled production history), but this movie is great for if you feel like you need forgiveness or if you feel like you've been slighted by life. This song is probably the best part of the movie (spoilers, I guess), and is just a great song to listen to about emotional healing. And if you read the comments, like I have, then I'm not alone in how I've been touched by this song. :)

~Dem Asian Dramas~

So, um, this one is a bit more of a girly recommendation, but it's cute so I'm gonna mention it anyway. It's called [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Little_Thing_Called_First_Love]A Little Thing Called First Love[/url]. It's about a dorky girl named Miao Miao (pronounced Meow Meow--I will never forget that name XD) who falls in love with the popular guy in her high school. The series documents her as she graduates high school and each of them pursuit their university degrees and just grow in life.

This series is the master of house music. The entire soundtrack is so mellow and chill that it feels like you could curl up in a warm blanket and fall asleep listening to it. This series also has some really positive messages in it that I was not expecting from a Chinese show. First of all, the main character is the oldest of two siblings, both girls (anyone remember the One-Child-Policy?). Also, in a part of the world that is [url=https://youtu.be/m7xWRrRk_cw?si=k1uoXZFPg5FtAeMz]obsessed with being underweight[/url], one of the main character's best friends is one of the best representations of overweight characters I've ever seen in media. She's always, unashamedly, on a diet, and her attitude is "if I make [my target weight], that's good; and if I don't, I'm fine with that." That is a downright BEAUTIFUL message to send to young girls in this day and age, and I'm all for it! :D She's also the only girl in the show that [i]doesn't[/i] have a love interest, so she kind of acts as the rational center for the other two girls, and helps keep them in check. Overall, a really positive character, and a great role model for young girls! :3

Also, I really like the male lead in this one. In most Asian Dramas, it's some variation of the Quirky Girl falls in love with the Stoic Man, and while there's a bit of that here, this guy is a lot softer (for lack of a better word) than the other Stoic Guys I've seen. Instead of being abrasive, stand-offish, and rude, he's genuinely kind, interested in the main character's life, and it totally makes sense why the main girl falls for him. The only thing that really puts him in the "Stoic Man" category is the fact that he's quiet, but apart from that, it's a refreshing change of pace for the genre!

And I suppose this is kind of a spoiler, but [spoiler]he should have proposed to her at the end. He didn't. [i]BUT HE TOTALLY SHOULD HAVE...![/i][/spoiler]

Anyway, that's all from me for now. Take care everyone! ^w^

So, after posting about the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/355520/view/3725085394629229792]last Asian Drama[/url], I felt like the biggest idiot ever because there was another Asian Drama that my mom and I had stumbled across that tackles the sexism dynamic as well, that we actually liked a lot better.

I'll get to the chase. The show is called [url=https://youtu.be/GRVpH4fF4jw]No Doubt in Us[/url], and is based on a Chinese Webtoon. (I checked the webtoon out, and I genuinely like the show better, so I'm recommending that one.) It's a story that takes place in Ye Olde RWBY Knock-Off China, where the Emperor has blonde hair and blue eyes, and candy-coloured hair abounds. The Emperor in question is a very smart bookworm type of guy, who is generally admired by the members of his family and the women in his harem...with one exception. Said exception being his wife, the Empress, who is a Strong Independent Woman™ who don't need no man. The two don't see eye to eye until, one day, they fall into their pond by accident, and somehow switch bodies. So now they have to team up to figure out how to switch back, all while navigating the political court as well as the family drama that neither one of them is prepared for.

Basically, it's [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freaky_Friday_(2003_film)]Freaky Friday[/url] in Ye Olde China. XD

All joking aside, this is series is surprisingly well written. I joked that the Empress is a Strong Independent Woman™, and she is, but for being of that archetype, she's [i]not[/i] obnoxious? She's from an influential military family and with two rough-and-tumble older brothers, so it makes sense that she'd be kind of a jock. The show also goes out of its way to show that she's the one of the only women who's like this, and the women of the royal court actually look down on her for being a "brute". And while she's not an airhead, it's also shown that she's not as smart as the other court members, which has led to her being taken advantage of and manipulated by people in the past. She's strong, but she's not invincible.

The bookworm Emperor is also well written as a character. I have less to say about him, but he's, by far, the smartest guy in the room at any given time, and can easily navigate through day-to-day situations through his wit and cunning alone. And what's a breath of fresh air is how the show deliberately goes out of its way to criticize both the Emperor AND the Empress. While I do feel like they criticize the Emperor [i]slightly[/i] more than the Empress, it's made [b]very[/b] clear that both of them need to change. The show really goes out of its way to show how the two characters compliment each other, and it's only through their teamwork that they're able to become the best versions of themselves. Which, you know, is a nuance lost in most North American storytelling these days. :P

I also appreciate how the body-swap thing happens between a husband and wife, so there's none of this "will-they-won't-they" nonsense that we have to sit through in most T.V. Shows. They're already a couple, so the main focus stays on the plot and only on the plot. It never feels like the audience's time is being wasted.

The episodes are ten minutes a pop, so they really go by quickly, but they never feel like they're rushed. There's a lot of wibbly-wobbly-timey-whimey logic that goes on when it comes to the magic system, but that's almost a given in any Historical Asian Drama you watch. The show also heavily relies on chibis, which I personally didn't mind, but my mom found them annoying. Overall, it's a well written show that deserves a lot more attention than its getting, and it does enough things right that I give it a double thumbs up. ːsteamthumbsupː ːsteamthumbsupː

One ruled by Male Chauvinists and the other ruled by Female Misandrists. The main guy in the story is a prince from Male Chauvinist Town and is sent off to go marry a princess of Female Misandrist Town. Things go awry in multiple ways.

notes.title: I Had Three Birthdays Last Year
notes.content:
So, my family is full of picky eaters. I used to be one of the worst ones until I started going to [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fViYK_Xb3Wg]Alpha[/url] and realized that it would be kind of embarrassing if I didn't eat what was put in front of me. I bring this up because often our tastes are very different at the dinner table, and sometimes when my mom and I want to eat at some place else, my dad will be like "whatever" and be fine with staying home.

Now, back in November, right before Remembrance Day, my mom and I wanted to go to this seafood restaurant that we don't go to very often, and this time we had decided to invite some friends from Church who lived in the area. So, we get to the lobster place, and they're sitting at a table, waiting for us (as you do). Then we sit down and get talking, and the people we're with hand me a birthday card. I thought it was nice, if not a bit strange, but we hadn't seen them in a long time, so I figured that was the reason for the late birthday card. It was when they handed me a small bouquet of flowers when I [i]really[/i] started to get weirded out.

Turns out, they thought it was my birthday that day, which it wasn't. And they had already told the waitress to prepare a dessert for me.

Whoops.

We get back to the waitress and tell her the misunderstanding, and explain that, [i]no, my birthday is in the summer,[/i] thank you. ːsteamlaughcryː I did have that dessert, but we paid for it, and had a good time all around.

We got home and told my dad about the whole thing. So, the very next evening, he invites my grandpa over, gets a cake out of nowhere, and explains that it's because it's my birthday. So we had another low-key birthday bash for me again that night.

And that is the story of how I had three birthdays in one year.

Can't get much better than that. ːsteamsunnyː

notes.title: BIG FAT MONDO UPDATE...With Some Terrible News...(Update Video #12)
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=zjSZwUDlrzY;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]...And just so some of you guys don't miss it, I'm going to write out my script from the video, directly into this announcement. >.> [i]*Ahem.*[/i]

I’m going to update my game! I can do that over winter break, right? :D

{SIX YEARS LATER…[b]LITERALLY[/b].}

[i]*Sobs relentlessly.*

*Cough.*[/i] Hiiii! A new update video! And a new YouTube Channel! …I forgot my password. It was really embarrassing...

But I’m BAAAACCCKKKKK! You’d thought you’d gotten rid of me, hadn’t you?! Nope! I’m still around! If you felt that took too long, then congratulations! You now know what it’s like to read one of my fanfics!

ANYWAY, it’s been a while! But I finally, finally, FINALLY finished my game! ...Again! Mostly! I…could kinda use a pixel artist or two to help me make my game not look like a blurry mess? And a programmer would be really, really nice too.

[i]*Cough.*[/i] So, what’s new? Well, first of all, after much deliberation, I’ve uploaded the revamp as it’s own individual game. (Don’t worry, though. You get the new game for free. [b][[u]EDIT[/u]] OR WILL YOU?![/b])

But, don’t worry. If you want to pay me more, then you totally can with the new Optional Additional Payment System! So now you can pay me exactly how much or how little you want! I’ve had WAY TOO MANY YEARS TO THINK ABOUT THIS, GUYS! But I THINK I’VE FINALLY FOUND A WAY TO MAKE ALL OF YOU HAPPY WITH THIS!

YOU’RE WELCOME.

[b][[u]EDIT[/u]]
Or that [i]was[/i] the plan. But then stupidity happened. Watch 1:39 to 3:27 in the video to see what I mean. Looks there is no possible way for me to give the game to all of you at the same time, like I had intended to. Sorry about that. As you can see, there is literally nothing I can do about it.

If you think you should get the revamp for free, like some of you have mentioned in the past, please send me a friend request so I can give you a Steam Key as compensation. Now back to what I had written before this had happened...[/b]

Since this revamp has been six years in the making, there are several portions of the game that were changed. (Obviously.) For the most part I tried not to censor anything, but some parts of the game have been heavily rewritten. For example, the Unworn Wedding Dress Quest is now given to you by Robert, instead of Ganguro. And I’ve completely dismantled the Frankfert Quest in favour of something a little more…logical? You'll see what I mean if you replay it.

With that said, with great rewrites come great new opportunities! So behold! A total of 24 new achievements have been added, which include 3 New Endings! Well, uh, sort of. One of them is just if you lose the Final Battle. But uh…the other two are completely new! So that’s something!

And let’s say you’re one of those people who encountered a teensy iddy biddy tiny winy glitch that caused the game to crash during the original. It wasn’t a big deal. It’s not like many of you found it or anything.

But, in the event that you were completely burned by how the old Battle System was, then worry no more! Introducing Pacifist Mode! The mode where you can skip almost every with the assumption that you win. And I say “almost” because you can’t use it during the Five Trials Quest. Or the insta-death battles. But apart from that, you can skip every single battle; including the bosses. Yes, you heard that right. All the bosses are now entirely optional. Because I know that, frankly, some of you have much better things to do with your time than spend three months grinding for some stupid battle you never really wanted to do in the first place...ULTIMA WEAPON.

This has actually been a new feature for a while now, as I added it just after my last video update. It was a feature that I was going to mention in the next update video, but, um…I didn't get around to making it until now.

Oh, and the game doesn’t break if you skim through the cutscenes, anymore. So now you can totally speedrun this game! FINALLY! JUST WHAT EVERYONE WAS ALWAYS ASKING! YOU CAN NOW DO SPEEDRUNS!

(Literally nobody was asking for this.)

And who knows? Maybe this version of the game won’t act up and corrupt video files of well-meaning Let's Players this time around!

…And if it makes your Anti-Virus go off, then I SWEAR, I’ll—

Anyway, I really do hope that my game is finished this time. Like, I’m not even you guys and even I think this is ridiculous. Like, I would, ideally, like to update the graphics and the program a little bit behind the scenes, but I can live with these things for now, because last April I was finally able to play the game from beginning to end without it crashing. Yes. It’s taken me THAT LONG to do that. I really, really want this game to be done so I can move on with my life!

But that doesn’t mean that you've necessarily heard the last from me. While working on the Revamp has kinda been my main priority, I have been working on some other stuff behind the scenes. [b]NOT VIDEOGAMES. I am kinda done with them right now because I am so frustrated.[/b] But I managed to put together a [url=https://www.webtoons.com/en/challenge/handsome-and-hideous/list?title_no=324693]Graphic Novel[/url], and I'm hoping to maybe, one day get two T.V. Shows out there? Maybe?

I would say I would want them on Netflix, except, um, Netflix doesn’t have the best reputation for that kind of thing. >.> *HackCoughCowboyBebopHackCough*

So, if you’ve enjoyed my game, I would appreciate it if you would help me out with my future endeavours. Honestly, that would mean the world to me.

Either way, sorry for the RIDICULOUSLY long delay, (and the fact that Steam refuses to let me give you free stuff for no discernible reason) but I hope the end result was worth it! Happy gaming~ :3
